clue.text: Exit 16 to require no explanation

parts.note: to exit is to go
the answer to 16 down is SILENTLY, which means much the same as this phrase

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction: leave quietly, because some things need no explaining.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay takes the solver to 16 down: 'Exit silently' is GO WITHOUT SAYING, read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: When something goes without saying it is so obvious that nobody needs to spell it out; the idiom is a fixed phrase.

clue.text: The theatrical profession includes one from long ago

definitions.note: the answer used attributively, as in Stone Age tools

indicators.note: something that includes another thing holds it inside itself

parts.note: the stage is the acting profession, as in 'go on the stage'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Acting as a trade is said to number among its members someone ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'The' belongs to the phrase 'the stage'; the profession takes ONE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as Stone Age is very old or primitive, belonging to the prehistoric period of stone tools.

clue.text: Hairstyle for a revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters before this word are turned into a new order

parts.note: the four letters of these two little words, rearranged

explanation.surface: A hairdo suited to a radical rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' looks like a noun for a rebel, but it is the signal to rearrange 'for a'.
explanation.definitionFit: An Afro is a rounded, bushy style of naturally tightly curled hair, popular with radicals in the 1960s and 1970s.

clue.text: Piece of hair of the dog left under the buss

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under something means coming below it, later in the light

parts.note: buss is an old word for a kiss
a cur is a mongrel dog
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A tuft from a dog's coat found beneath a kiss, with a nod to 'hair of the dog'.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'under' places the dog and left beneath the kiss. 'Hair of the dog' is a hangover cure, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss curl is a small curl of hair pressed flat on the forehead or cheek, so it is one small piece of hair.

clue.text: A gadabout before 10 goes slowly

parts.note: taken as written
read as gad about: the word gad turned about
the digits 1 and 0 drawn as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: Someone who loves going out, arriving before ten, moves at a leisurely pace.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is the number, not clue 10, shown by its digits as letters; 'before' puts it after A and the turned gad.
explanation.definitionFit: Adagio is the Italian musical direction to play slowly, used as an adverb in scores and concert programmes.

clue.text: Pacific area, home: hunt round it first

definitions.note: the answer is a sea within the Pacific

indicators.note: first says the hunt with home inside comes at the front, ahead of the remaining piece
the hunt goes round the word for home, enclosing it

parts.note: to hunt is to chase
at home is in
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A spot in the Pacific, a home, and a chase that circles it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' says the hunt round home comes before area, which supplies the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: The China Sea, East and South, is a marginal sea of the western Pacific Ocean, so it is part of the Pacific.

clue.text: Former minister: odd he didn't finish

indicators.note: not finishing means the word stops short of its last letter

parts.note: odd means strange

explanation.surface: A one-time government minister who curiously left his work incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: Gavin Strang was a Labour minister, in charge of transport in Tony Blair's first cabinet until 1998.
explanation.definitionFit: Gavin Strang served as a minister in Blair's government and had been sacked by the time of this puzzle, hence former.

clue.text: Article in the Financial Times, sadly working in guineas, shows itês all over

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the article sits in the newspaper's initials, inside them
sadly here is treated as a word gone wrong, so its own letters are muddled

parts.note: FT is the standard short form of the Financial Times
a is the indefinite article
this word's own five letters, rearranged
a machine that is working is in operation, or in
G is the abbreviation for guinea, an old coin worth 21 shillings, so two of them make GS

explanation.surface: A gloomy business-paper article, priced in old coin, announces that everything has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' is both indicator and its own fodder. The answer is from the saying 'it ain't over till the fat lady sings', from opera. The clue shows 'itês' where the paper printed 'it's'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the saying, the fat lady singing marks the true end of an opera, so the phrase signals that a contest is finished.

clue.text: See 14
Marry at a church which is on strike?

parts.note: to strike is to hit
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A wedding held at a church whose workers have walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On strike' looks like an industrial dispute; here the church is placed on, after, the word for strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To hitch, as in getting hitched, is an informal verb for getting married or joining two people together.

clue.text: No use getting upset after soldier retreats from fire

indicators.note: after sends the jumbled letters behind the soldier, so they come second
retreating means going backwards, so the soldier is read in reverse

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so those letters are jumbled

parts.note: the five letters of these words, rearranged

explanation.surface: It is pointless being distressed once a soldier pulls back from the line of fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the rearranged letters behind the reversed soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous rock forms from molten magma, and the word comes from Latin ignis, so igneous means produced by heat or volcanic origin.

clue.text: Literary wizard produces acceleration plus 50 per cent, vulgarly

parts.note: g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity
plus means and
50 per cent is half, and said vulgarly the h is dropped

explanation.surface: A recipe for a wizard: some speed, plus a coarse-sounding half.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the h is a mark of a working-class London accent, which 'vulgarly' asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: Gandalf is the wizard in Tolkien's novels The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, a famous figure of fiction.

clue.text: Top man on commercial

parts.note: a man is he
a commercial is an advertisement, an ad

explanation.surface: The chief executive appearing in a television advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top man' reads as one phrase for a boss, but the definition is only 'Top'.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of something is its top, as in the head of a page, a table, or a staircase.

clue.text: "What the eye doesn't see …" — blind and crazy?

parts.note: a blind hides things, putting them where they cannot be seen
someone crazy is said to be out of their mind

explanation.surface: Quoting an old saying, then asking whether it describes someone sightless and mad.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes the start of a different saying, 'what the eye doesn't see, the heart doesn't grieve over', which makes the same point.
explanation.definitionFit: Both proverbs say that people stop caring about things they no longer notice, so one stands for the other.

clue.text: Turn to numbers 1 and 50 — that should serve a purpose

parts.note: a U-turn, or simply U, is a turn
tens are numbers
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn to particular numbered pages, said to be useful.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description, not a synonym: a thing made for a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A utensil is a tool or container, especially in a kitchen, made for a practical use.

clue.text: Like an ass holding 10 oddly like a mouse?

indicators.note: done oddly, the letters of the number are put in a strange order
holding means having something inside, gripped within

parts.note: an ass is a fool, so like an ass is silly
the number ten written as a word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A comparison of a donkey and a mouse, with a number thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is the number, not a cross-reference to clue 10: spell it out as a word and rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quiet as a mouse is the stock simile, so like a mouse means making no noise.

clue.text: Moses fled after God started mad dispersal

indicators.note: dispersal scatters things, so the letters of the word are scattered into a new order
fled comes after the divine initial, so it is placed second
where God started means only the opening letter of that word is used

parts.note: the first letter of the word
fled means ran
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: A Biblical scene: Moses running away, with God and madness mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: Moses is not the prophet: Grandma Moses was a self-taught American folk painter who began painting in her seventies.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Mary Robertson Moses was universally known by the nickname Grandma Moses, so the nickname's first word stands with her surname.

clue.text: Warning to streetwalkers of Spooner's fatty glutinous mess

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of two words are exchanged

parts.note: fatty is lardy and a glutinous mess is goo; swap the opening sounds of the pair

explanation.surface: A cry of alarm to prostitutes, about a sticky greasy muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Streetwalkers here are just pedestrians. The answer was the cry of old Edinburgh before slops were thrown from upstairs windows, from French 'gardez l'eau', mind the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The cry warned people walking in the street below that dirty water was about to be emptied onto them.

clue.text: Hence come waves without water round an opening

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, enclosing it

parts.note: having no water is dry
a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: A riddle about waves that come from somewhere with no sea at all, around a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The waves are radio waves: Daventry, a Northamptonshire town far from the sea, was home to the BBC's famous long-wave transmitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasts went out from the BBC transmitting station at Daventry for decades, so radio signals came from there.

clue.text: Booty left by destroyer of game?

parts.note: booty is the spoils of war
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Plunder abandoned by a warship, a destroyer, which might have hunted game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Destroyer' suggests a warship, which fits the booty and port; the question mark flags a playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport ruins other people's fun, so such a person literally spoils the game for everyone.

clue.text: Player with piece of wood gets up to holding a French one

indicators.note: holding means having something gripped inside
in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
one refers back to piece of wood, and the French word for wood is bois

explanation.surface: A musician with a stick of timber rises to grip a French one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of wood' is part of the definition, an instrument made of wood, and also the thing 'one' refers to.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, a woodwind instrument traditionally made of wood, so plays a piece of wood.

clue.text: Request for quiet let?

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
to let a property is to lease it

explanation.surface: Asking for a property to be let quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' looks like a verb meaning allow; here it is renting.
explanation.definitionFit: Please, as in 'please do', is the word with which a polite request is made.

clue.text: Where Henri IV succeeded the king in the bush?

indicators.note: the king is placed in the bush, inside it

parts.note: ivy is a climbing evergreen, an ivy bush
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A history question about where a French king won, slipping in a hidden monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Henri IV of France beat the Catholic League at the Battle of Ivry in 1590; the roman IV also sits inside the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivry, in Normandy, is where Henri IV defeated the forces of the Catholic League in battle in 1590.

clue.text: West African capital slightly changed …

indicators.note: changed a little means the letters are reworked, with only a small alteration

parts.note: the ellipsis runs on into 24 across, whose answer is the starting point

explanation.surface: The name of an African city, said to be close to something we say.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs on into 24 across: swap the final I of YOU AND I for E and move the A forward. The printed grid's YYOUNDE is a typo for Yaoundé.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaoundé is the capital city of Cameroon, on the west coast of central Africa.

clue.text: … from the vowel sounds we make

indicators.note: sounds means the vowels are taken for what they sound like when spoken

parts.note: two vowel letters, U and I, said as names of letters

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: the vowels people produce when talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters U and I, said aloud, are pronouns; together they mean 'we'.
explanation.definitionFit: We is the pronoun covering the speaker together with the person addressed, the two people meant by the phrase.

clue.text: Somewhat run-down ruin

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of something, so the letters are a piece of the following word

parts.note: the middle of this word, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: Something partly dilapidated is falling into decay.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo someone or something is to bring about their downfall or ruin, as in 'pride was his undoing'.

clue.text: Consonantal sound of North American girl

parts.note: NA is the abbreviation for North American
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: The way an American girl pronounces her consonants.
explanation.definitionFit: A nasal is a speech sound such as m, n or ng made with air passing through the nose, a consonant class.

clue.text: Weapon holder, a Southern term for an amphibian

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a term is a word
a frog is an amphibian

explanation.surface: A claim that in the South people have a special name for a frog.
explanation.walkthrough: A frog is also a loop on a belt that carries a sword or bayonet, which is why the pieces read so naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword frog is the belt attachment from which a sword scabbard hangs, so it holds the weapon.
